source_name: Career/news pages of individual MK banks (generic pattern: NLB, Komercijalna, Sparkasse, Halkbank, ProCredit, ЦКБ, ALTA, Развојна банка МБДП)
why_relevant: Each licensed MK bank runs its own careers/news section; these are the authoritative originals behind aggregator reposts, and state-owned Развојна банка (MBDP) additionally publishes procurement-adjacent notices. Building a per-bank watchlist is the backbone of this cell; only MBDP's URL is asserted here because the others were not directly observed in this run.

source_name: NLB Banka Skopje - LinkedIn company page (and MK bank/vendor LinkedIn pages generally)
why_relevant: LinkedIn job posts and employee-role changes are often the very first public trace of a platform programme (e.g. a bank suddenly hiring 'Temenos consultant' or 'ISO 20022 migration lead'), and vendor pages announce MK wins before local press. Also reveals which integrator staff sit inside which bank.

source_name: Македонска банкарска асоцијација (МБА) - Соопштенија и Активности
why_relevant: The industry association announces sector events, working commissions and joint initiatives (e.g. sector-wide move to strong customer authentication from 1 March 2026). A sector-wide regulatory/technical deadline announced by MBA is a reliable predictor of near-simultaneous procurement at multiple banks. Its commissions also reveal which topics banks are coordinating on.

source_name: КИБС АД Скопје (Клириншка куќа) - корпоративен сајт и настани
why_relevant: National clearing house and payment-system operator; also a digital-trust and ICT service provider. It hosted the EACHA annual conference in Skopje (20 May 2026, ~200 participants from 30 countries, with global IT/consulting companies present) and obtained an instant-payments licence - both are strong precursors of bank-side integration projects and vendor selection. Its own news announces which partners implemented what (e.g. OneID/SignPlus with Nextsens for Sparkasse).

source_name: EACHA annual conference (Skopje edition) - agenda / sponsor coverage
why_relevant: Coverage of the EACHA 2026 Skopje conference names the institutions and vendor types in the room and the themes (account-to-account digital payments, ISO alignment). Which global IT/consulting firms travel to Skopje for this is a direct read on who is positioning for MK payment-infrastructure work.

source_name: MicroBalkans 2026 (regional financial-sector conference, Skopje)
why_relevant: Third edition of a Skopje conference drawing 200+ financial-sector representatives from 15 European countries, explicitly targeting non-bank financial institutions, microcredit institutions, savings houses, banks, fintech and IT companies, investors and regulators. Sponsor/exhibitor rosters of exactly this kind of event flag vendors courting MK buyers ahead of tenders.

source_name: Асоцијација за е-трговија на Македонија (ecommerce.mk) - регионална конференција за е-трговија
why_relevant: Organiser of the annual Regional E-commerce Conference (9th edition, 3 Nov 2026, Skopje) with published gold/silver sponsor tiers; payment acquirers, PSPs and card processors buy those slots. Also republishes payment-licensing news (e.g. KIBS instant-payments licence). Sponsor tiers are a cheap proxy for which vendors are investing in MK market entry.

source_name: МАСИТ - Комора за информатичка и комуникациска технологија (годишна конференција + именик на членки)
why_relevant: The MK ICT chamber's annual conference (20th edition, 'MASIT 2.0 Recode Reality', 300+ participants) publishes sponsor/patron lists, and its member directory is the actor map of MK IT vendors and integrators - the supply side that bids on bank tenders. Sponsorship of a chamber event by a payments vendor is a market-entry tell.

source_name: Стопанска комора на Северна Македонија - Здружение за информатичка технологија
why_relevant: The national chamber's IT association organises sector events, B2B meetings and working groups where banks state technology intentions publicly. Chamber event announcements and member lists are a second, independent actor-map and event-calendar source alongside MASIT.

source_name: IT.mk форум - теми за финтек и плаќања
why_relevant: MK IT community forum with long-running fintech/payments threads (e.g. KEKS Pay Macedonia, 'Финтек револуција во Македонија'). Practitioners discuss which bank is migrating what, often citing internal or pre-announcement knowledge. Low credibility individually, high value as a lead generator for verification elsewhere.

source_name: Народна банка на РСМ - конкурси, награди и соопштенија за модернизација на МИПС
why_relevant: Beyond formal tenders, the central bank publishes annual award competitions (Годишна награда на НБРСМ), research calls and programme-progress statements - e.g. that modernisation of the Macedonian Interbank Payment System (МИПС) is advancing with EU support. A published modernisation programme is the strongest single predictor of downstream bank-side procurement across the whole market.

source_name: Македонска берза - годишна конференција (агенда, спонзори, панелисти)
why_relevant: The stock exchange's annual conference (24th edition, bilingual mk/en) is a fixture where banks, the MBA and financial-infrastructure vendors appear as speakers and sponsors. Agenda topics chosen by banks signal their next-year technology and regulatory priorities.

source_name: International vendor press-release wires covering MK bank wins (e.g. Entrust / BCS North Macedonia at Komercijalna banka)
why_relevant: Global vendors announce MK deals on international wires before or instead of MK media - here Entrust with local partner BCS North Macedonia delivering card digitisation and push provisioning to Google Wallet at Komercijalna banka. These releases name the local implementation partner, which is exactly the actor set that bids on subsequent tenders, and a wallet/tokenisation win at one bank reliably precedes peer-bank projects.

source_name: Thebanks.eu - профили на банки во Северна Македонија (actor map)
why_relevant: Aggregated list and profiles of MK banks; useful as the seed list for building the per-bank careers/news watchlist that this cell depends on. Not a signal source itself, purely a pointer/actor-map utility (authoritative list should still be taken from NBRM).

source_name: NLB d.d. — Javni razpisi (public calls / tenders, Slovenian parent of NLB Banka Skopje)
why_relevant: Group parent NLB d.d. publishes public calls/notices in Slovenian. NLB Group runs group-level standards and vendor relationships that cascade to NLB Banka AD Skopje (NLB holds ~86.97%); parent-level calls are the earliest visible signal of vendor selection that later lands in MK.

source_name: NLB Group corporate site (group markets / subsidiary structure incl. NLB Banka Skopje)
why_relevant: Establishes the ownership/control chain and which group entities exist, which is the prerequisite for tracing where an MK contract is actually decided. Group annual reports on the same estate disclose IT/digital programme rollouts across subsidiaries.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (EGP / s ProServ) — supplier onboarding and supplier documents
why_relevant: Sparkasse Banka AD Skopje sits under the Steiermärkische Sparkasse / Sparkassen-Erste orbit. EGP is the group's centralised supply-management arm in Vienna, publishing Supplier Code of Conduct, NDAs, audit questionnaires and scorecards translated into national languages — i.e. the gatekeeping rules any vendor to the MK subsidiary must pass.

source_name: Steiermärkische Sparkasse — corporate site / Sparkassengruppe institute list
why_relevant: Direct parent-side estate for Sparkasse Bank MK. Useful for confirming which group service companies (IT, cards, processing) are shared across the Verbund and therefore likely to be imposed on the Skopje subsidiary rather than tendered locally.

source_name: Halkbank T.A.Ş. (Türkiye) — Duyurular / Haberler ve Duyurular
why_relevant: Halkbank AD Skopje's Turkish parent. Group-level announcements (technology programmes, subsidiary investments) are published here in Turkish before any MK-side visibility. Observed announcement streams are dominated by real-estate/foreclosure auctions, so signal density for IT/payments procurement is low but non-zero.

source_name: EKAP — Elektronik Kamu Alımları Platformu (Turkish public procurement platform, tender search)
why_relevant: Halkbank T.A.Ş. is Turkish state-controlled; procurement by Turkish public-sector entities is published on EKAP/ihale.gov.tr. A group-level IT or payments award to a Turkish contracting entity is the leading indicator of what later appears in the Skopje subsidiary. Requires verification that Halkbank publishes as a contracting entity there.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Georgia — Tenders section (regional sibling procurement pattern)
why_relevant: ProCredit group subsidiaries publish their own tender pages (Georgia, Ukraine observed). The tender templates, scope wording and evaluation criteria are group-standardised, so sibling-country notices reveal the specification patterns ProCredit Bank AD Skopje will use even when MK-side notices are not published.

source_name: Opentender.eu (DIGIWHIST / Government Transparency Institute) — North Macedonia portal
why_relevant: A cross-border, standing ARCHIVE of national procurement data for 35 jurisdictions including North Macedonia, harvested from national portals and TED. This is the single strongest answer to the 'notices removed from the MK portal after expiry' problem — historical MK notices and awards persist here in structured form.

source_name: Internet Archive Wayback CDX Server API — e-nabavki.gov.mk capture index
why_relevant: Directly addresses the cell's archived/expired-notice angle: a CDX query against the MK e-procurement domain returns a capture index stretching back to 2007, letting expired or removed notice pages be recovered by timestamp. Confirmed to return data for this domain during scouting (liveness to be re-verified by the deterministic pass).
